patterns.pattern: What is your favorite wild animal? - My favorite wild animal is the [animal].
patterns.vi: Động vật hoang dã yêu thích của bạn là gì? - Động vật hoang dã yêu thích của tớ là...
examples: What is your favorite wild animal? - My favorite wild animal is the panda.
What is your favorite wild animal? - My favorite wild animal is the dolphin.
What is your favorite wild animal? - My favorite wild animal is the eagle.

patterns.pattern: Where do [animals] live? - They live in the [habitat].
patterns.vi: Các con [vật] sống ở đâu? - Chúng sống ở [môi trường sống].
examples: Where do lions live? - They live in the jungle.
Where do dolphins live? - They live in the ocean.
Where do penguins live? - They live in snowy icy places.
A cheetah is faster than a lion.
An elephant is bigger than a zebra.
A giraffe is taller than a rhino.

patterns.pattern: What are the [animals] doing? - They are [V-ing].
patterns.vi: Những con [vật] đang làm gì? - Chúng đang...
examples: What are the monkeys doing? - They are climbing trees.
What are the dolphins doing? - They are jumping high.
What are the eagles doing? - They are flying in the sky.

patterns.pattern: What can a [animal] do? - It can [action].
patterns.vi: Một con [vật] có thể làm gì? - Nó có thể...
examples: What can a kangaroo do? - It can hop very high.
What can an eagle do? - It can see fish from far away.
What can a tiger do? - It can run fast and swim well.

patterns.vi: Hôm qua, chúng tớ đã thăm [nơi chốn] và nhìn thấy [các con vật].
examples: Yesterday, we visited the zoo and saw two big elephants.
Yesterday, we visited the wildlife park and saw cute pandas.
Yesterday, we visited the natural reserve and saw wild birds.

patterns.pattern: We will [action] to protect wild animals.
patterns.vi: Chúng tớ sẽ [hành động] để bảo vệ động vật hoang dã.
examples: We will draw posters to protect wild animals.
We will keep the forest clean to protect wild animals.
We will learn more about nature to protect wild animals.

patterns.pattern: Could you see any [animals] in the wild? - Yes, I could. / No, I couldn't.
patterns.vi: Bạn có thể đã nhìn thấy con [vật] nào ngoài tự nhiên không? - Có, tớ có. / Không, tớ không.
examples: Could you see any dolphins in the sea? - Yes, I could.
Could you see any bears in the forest? - No, I couldn't.
Could you see any eagles in the sky? - Yes, I could.

grammar.title: Comparatives with Short Adjectives
grammar.explain_en: We add -er to short adjectives to compare two animals or things. We use 'than' after the adjective.
grammar.explain_vi: Chúng ta thêm đuôi -er vào sau tính từ ngắn để so sánh hai con vật hoặc đồ vật. Dùng 'than' sau tính từ.
examples: A cheetah is faster than a lion.
An elephant is heavier than a hippo.
A giraffe is taller than a horse.
grammar.right: ✅ A cheetah is faster than a tiger.
grammar.wrong: ❌ A cheetah is more fast than a tiger.

grammar.title: Present Continuous for Animal Actions
grammar.explain_en: We use is/are + verb-ing to describe actions happening right now.
grammar.explain_vi: Chúng ta dùng is/are + động từ-ing để tả hành động của các con vật đang diễn ra ngay lúc này.
examples: The monkey is eating a banana.
The birds are flying over the trees.
The lions are sleeping under the sun.
grammar.right: ✅ The monkeys are swinging on trees.
grammar.wrong: ❌ The monkeys is swing on trees.

grammar.title: Past Simple with Was / Were and Regular/Irregular Verbs
grammar.explain_en: We use the Past Simple to talk about completed trips and events in the past.
grammar.explain_vi: Chúng ta dùng thì Quá khứ đơn để kể lại những chuyến đi hoặc sự việc đã hoàn thành trong quá khứ.
examples: I was at the safari park yesterday.
We saw three giant pandas.
The elephants walked slowly to the water.
grammar.right: ✅ We visited the zoo last Sunday.
grammar.wrong: ❌ We visit the zoo last Sunday.

grammar.title: Abilities with Can and Could
grammar.explain_en: Use 'can' for present ability and 'could' for past ability or polite questions.
grammar.explain_vi: Dùng 'can' để nói về khả năng ở hiện tại và 'could' để nói về khả năng trong quá khứ hoặc câu hỏi lịch sự.
examples: Dolphins can swim very fast.
When I was young, I could not name all the wild animals.
Could you see the eagles high in the sky yesterday?
grammar.right: ✅ She could see the tigers at the park yesterday.
grammar.wrong: ❌ She can saw the tigers at the park yesterday.

readings.title: A Day at the Wildlife Park
readings.text: Yesterday, Nam and his family visited a big wildlife park near their town. The weather was sunny and warm. They saw many amazing wild animals living in open areas. First, they looked at two giant elephants drinking water near a stream. Next, they saw three tall giraffes eating green leaves high in the trees. Nam liked the pandas best because they were fluffy and cute. A young panda was eating bamboo happily. Nam took many pictures with his camera. He felt very happy to see wild animals living in a safe and green environment.

readings.title: The Smart Ocean Mammals
readings.text: Dolphins and whales are remarkable wild mammals that live in oceans across the world. Although they live underwater, they are not fish. They breathe air through blowholes on top of their heads. Dolphins are famous for being smart and friendly. They can jump high out of the water and perform playful tricks. In addition, dolphins use special clicking sounds to talk to each other and navigate underwater. Whales are much bigger than dolphins. In fact, the blue whale is the largest animal on Earth! It is even bigger than the biggest dinosaur that ever lived. Unfortunately, ocean pollution and trash harm these wonderful creatures. Today, young students around the world are working together to clean up beaches so ocean animals can swim safely.

readings.title: Protecting Our Wild Friends and Their Habitats
readings.text:
Every wild animal plays a special role in nature. Lions and tigers keep the forests balanced by hunting weaker animals. Elephants create pathways through dense jungles that help smaller animals walk easily. Monkeys help plant new trees by dropping seeds across the tropical forest floor. However, many wild animals are in danger today because people are cutting down forests to build cities and farms.

When trees disappear, wild animals lose their natural habitats and food sources. For example, giant pandas struggle to find bamboo forests, while cheetahs lose wide grasslands for hunting. Furthermore, illegal hunting makes many species rare and endangered. If we do not act now, some beautiful animals will vanish forever.

Fortunately, children and adults can take simple steps to save wildlife. We can reduce plastic waste, plant more trees, and support national parks. Schools can organize eco-friendly events to teach students about nature. Last week, Mai's class created colorful posters about endangered tigers. Next month, they will plant twenty young trees in their school garden. When we protect nature, we protect all living things on Earth.

listening.script: Hello everyone! Welcome to Nature World Radio. Today, ranger Tom is telling us about his trip to the tropical jungle. Last week, Tom walked deep into the green forest. Early in the morning, he saw three noisy monkeys swinging in the high trees. They were eating sweet yellow fruits. Near the river, Tom saw a big crocodile resting on the warm sand. It was very quiet. Then, Tom heard a loud sound in the bushes. A strong tiger was walking slowly through the tall grass! Tom stayed very quiet and took three beautiful photos. Tom says that jungle animals need big, clean forests to live safely. Next month, Tom will visit an ocean bay to study wild dolphins. Let me know if you want to join our junior ranger club!

life_skill.title: PROTECT WILD ANIMALS AND NATURE
life_skill.intro: Wild animals are an essential part of our natural world. By protecting their forest and ocean homes, we keep our planet healthy and beautiful!
life_skill.intro_vi: Động vật hoang dã là một phần thiết yếu của thế giới tự nhiên. Bằng cách bảo vệ ngôi nhà rừng núi và đại dương của chúng, chúng ta giữ cho hành tinh luôn xanh sạch đẹp!
can_do: Never throw trash or plastic in forests, rivers, or beaches.
Plant trees and flowers in the school garden.
Learn about endangered wild animals and share knowledge with friends.
Turn off lights and save water at home.
Do not buy toys made from wild animal parts.
Support national parks and wildlife conservation funds.
Use reusable bags instead of single-use plastic bags.
Be quiet and respectful when visiting nature parks.
Keep local lakes and streams clean.
Recycle paper to save forest trees.
Draw posters to encourage people to protect wildlife.
Always treat all living creatures with love and kindness.

classroom_game.name: Animal Action Freeze
steps_en: The teacher plays lively music and calls out a wild animal action (e.g., 'Swinging monkeys!' or 'Hopping kangaroos!').
Students move around the classroom pretending to be that animal.
When the music stops, students must freeze like animal statues.
The teacher asks a frozen student: 'What can your animal do?' or 'Is your animal bigger than a cat?'
The student answers using unit sentence structures to win points for their team.
steps_vi: Giáo viên bật nhạc sôi động và hô tên hành động của con vật (ví dụ: 'Khỉ chuyền cành!' hoặc 'Chuột túi nhảy!').
Học sinh di chuyển quanh lớp học đóng giả làm con vật đó.
Khi nhạc dừng, học sinh phải đóng băng như những bức tượng con vật.
Giáo viên hỏi một học sinh: 'Con vật của em có thể làm gì?' hoặc 'Con vật của em có to hơn con mèo không?'
Học sinh trả lời bằng cấu trúc câu đã học để giành điểm cho đội của mình.
